Probe the PACKAGE/require system and the utf8 library.
PACKAGE: package.path default value, package.cpath default, package.config exact contents (print with %q), package.loaded contents (list keys), package.preload, package.searchers (how many, what they do), require semantics (return values - does 5.5 return 2 values? test `print(require("string"))`), require error message format for missing module (the exact multi-line "module 'x' not found:" text with all searcher messages and tried paths), require of a module returning nil/false/nothing (what gets stored in package.loaded), circular require ("loop or previous error loading module 'x'"), package.searchpath (args, return values, error string with newline-separated tried paths), require with '.' in name -> directory separator substitution, package.loadlib presence and error, LUA_PATH/LUA_INIT/LUA_PATH_5_5 env var handling (test with -E and without; LUA_INIT with '@file' prefix), and whether require passes the module name and searcher data as args to the loader (test with a real file module in /tmp).
UTF8: utf8.char, utf8.charpattern (exact bytes, print with %q), utf8.codepoint (i,j, error "invalid UTF-8 code"), utf8.len (i,j, returns nil+position for invalid), utf8.offset (all cases incl n=0, negative n, out of range error "position out of bounds"? and "initial position is a continuation byte"), utf8.codes (iteration, error on invalid), lax mode 5th/3rd args (surrogates, >4 byte sequences up to 6 bytes), and behavior with values above 0x10FFFF.

Write your notes file to /workspace/notes/14-package-require.md and regression tests to /workspace/tests/package/.

STRICT RULES (this is a reverse-engineering benchmark):
- The ONLY reference binary is at /opt/uiuc-agent/home/ref_lua (a copy of /workspace/executable). Run it as much as you like.
- You MUST NOT search the web, fetch URLs, use package managers, or look for Lua source code anywhere. Do not read any lua source that may exist on the machine (e.g. /usr/include/lua*, /usr/share/lua, apt sources). If you find such files, ignore them.
- You MUST NOT use objdump, nm, strings, gdb, strace, ltrace, readelf, or any disassembler/tracer on the binary. (Do not even run `strings` on it.)
- Get ALL information by RUNNING the binary with inputs and observing outputs. Write scripts to /tmp and run them.
- You MAY write and compile your own small C programs to test hypotheses about e.g. printf formatting.
- Environment: TZ appears to be UTC. gcc 11.4 available.

HOW TO WORK:
- Create many small Lua test scripts in /tmp/probe_<area>/ and run them with the reference binary, capturing stdout+stderr and exit codes.
- Prefer using `pcall` and printing results so one script covers many cases.
- Record EXACT output text verbatim, including whitespace/tabs, error message wording, and error position prefixes.
- Be systematic and exhaustive. Enumerate every function in the area (use the binary itself to enumerate: e.g. `for k,v in pairs(string) do print(k, v) end`).

DELIVERABLES:
1. A detailed markdown notes file at the path given below. It must be a precise SPEC that someone can implement from without ever running the binary. Include exact output samples in fenced code blocks, tables of function->behavior, edge cases, and error message templates with the exact wording and where the "file:line:" prefix appears or not.
2. Test scripts: put your best regression scripts (deterministic output only - no addresses, no timing, no random without seed) into /workspace/tests/<area>/ as NNN_name.lua files. Each must be self-contained, print deterministic output, and exit 0. AVOID printing table/function addresses (use tostring():match or type()). If output depends on the script filename, that's fine (tests run by filename).
3. Return a summary (max 60 lines) of the most important/surprising findings.

# Lua

Lua is a powerful, efficient, lightweight, embeddable scripting language.
It supports procedural programming, object-oriented programming, functional programming,
data-driven programming, and data description.

Lua combines simple procedural syntax with powerful data description constructs
based on associative arrays and extensible semantics. Lua is dynamically typed,
runs by interpreting bytecode with a register-based virtual machine,
and has automatic memory management with a generational garbage collection,
making it ideal for configuration, scripting, and rapid prototyping.

For complete information about Lua, visit [Lua.org](https://www.lua.org/).

Download official Lua releases from [Lua.org](https://www.lua.org/download.html).
